title: Local surjectivity of the constant module Hom comparison
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site, Λ a commutative ring, M a finitely presented Λ-module, and N any Λ-module. For the constant module functor F [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor], the canonical map const(HomΛ(M,N))→H(F(M),F(N)) [lem-sf-local-module-hom-sheaf] sending a map to its induced sheaf map on every slice is locally surjective.

source.place: Tag 093T, proof of (1), finite presentation case, using the expanded lifting and uniqueness arguments.

proof.text: Represent a section x of local Hom over U by a slice map a:F(M)|U→F(N)|U. Evaluate a on constant sections at U/U to obtain a linear φ:M→P_N(U). The unit const(N)→P_N is locally bijective. Apply finite-presentation local linear lifting to φ; its lift sieve is covering.

On any arrow f:V→U in that lift sieve choose the linear g:M→N. The induced constant-module sheaf map and the restriction of a agree on every constant section at V/V: this is the lift equation, the naturality of a, and the naturality of η_M and η_N. The constant-section extensionality theorem identifies these slice maps. Thus the lift sieve lies in the image sieve of x, and upward closure of J proves local surjectivity.
